examples.en: After sitting for a long time, my leg went numb.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 남의 아픔에 너무 무감각해요.
examples.en: That person is too insensitive to others' pain.
It was so cold that my fingertips went numb.
He keeps looking out the window with a blank expression.

examples.ko: 나쁜 소식에 자꾸 무감각해지는 게 무서워요.
examples.en: I am scared that I keep becoming numb to bad news.
If the numbness lasts long, go to a hospital.

explain: 몸에서는 느낌이 없는 상태에, 마음에서는 남의 일에 아무 느낌이 없는 상태에 써요. '무관심'은 관심을 두지 않는 태도이고, '무감각'은 느끼는 힘이 둔한 상태예요. 보통 '무감각하다', '무감각해지다'로 써요.

phrases.en: Hearing it every day, I became numb to such words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자꾸 겪어서 느낌이 점점 없어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you gradually stop feeling something from repeated exposure.

phrases.example: 그는 친구의 말을 무감각하게 듣고 있었어요.
phrases.en: He was listening to his friend's words without feeling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무 느낌 없는 태도로 행동할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes acting with no feeling at all.

phrases.en: It's so cold that my hands have no feeling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 느낌이 없을 때 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say a body part has lost feeling.

explain_en: For the body it means no feeling; for the mind it means feeling nothing about others' matters. '무관심' is an attitude of not caring, while '무감각' is a dulled ability to feel. Usually used as '무감각하다' or '무감각해지다'.

en: being on the brink of death; deadly situation; being near death

examples.en: He hovered between life and death after a traffic accident.

examples.ko: 환자가 사경에 놓여서 가족들이 병원을 지켰어요.
examples.en: The patient was in critical condition, so the family stayed at the hospital.
The patient who came back from the brink recognized his family.
Grandfather, who had been near death, fortunately woke up.
I got lost in the mountains and was in mortal danger.

examples.ko: 큰 수술을 받고도 한동안 사경을 넘나들었어요.
examples.en: Even after major surgery, he went back and forth near death for a while.

explain: 죽을 고비를 말하고, 보통 '사경을 헤매다'처럼 정해진 꼴로 나와요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '죽을 뻔했어요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그는 큰 사고를 당하고 며칠 동안 사경을 헤맸어요.
phrases.en: hover between life and death
phrases.nuance_ko: 목숨이 위태로워서 살지 죽을지 알 수 없는 상태가 이어지는 모습이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes a stretch of time when someone's life is in danger and could go either way. It appears often in news and writing.

explain_en: It refers to a life-or-death crisis and usually appears in the fixed form '사경을 헤매다'. You see it in news and writing, while in everyday talk people say '죽을 뻔했어요' (I almost died).

examples.ko: 사고 후 식물인간이 되었던 환자가 깨어났어요.
examples.en: A patient who had been in a vegetative state after an accident woke up.

examples.ko: 그 환자는 식물인간 상태로 오 년을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The patient spent five years in a vegetative state.

examples.ko: 식물인간을 돌보는 가족의 어려움을 다룬 기사예요.
examples.en: It's an article about the hardships of families who care for patients in a vegetative state.
This movie is about a patient in a vegetative state and a nurse.
Could a family's voice help even a person in a vegetative state?
The family of a person in a vegetative state needs help from those around them.

explain: 뇌가 크게 다쳐서 의식이 없지만 숨은 쉬는 환자를 가리키는 말로 뉴스나 영화에서 나와요. 의학에서는 '식물 상태'라고도 해요. 사람을 낮춰 보는 느낌이 있을 수 있어서, 환자를 직접 이렇게 부르지는 않아요.

phrases.example: 큰 사고로 식물인간이 된 환자가 있어요.
phrases.en: There is a patient who fell into a vegetative state after a major accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뇌 손상으로 의식이 없어지는 상태가 되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone enters a state of unconsciousness due to brain damage.
phrases.en_equiv: to fall into a vegetative state

phrases.en: He is in the hospital in a vegetative state.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 대신 상태를 말해서 조금 더 조심스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state rather than the person, so it is somewhat more careful.

phrases.en: The doctor explained that the patient is in a vegetative state.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의학에서 쓰는 말이라 '식물인간'보다 중립적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A medical term that is more neutral than 식물인간.

explain_en: It appears in news and films for a patient with serious brain damage who has no consciousness but still breathes. In medicine it is also called '식물 상태'. It can sound demeaning, so people don't call a patient this directly.

examples.ko: 무서운 영화를 보다가 오금이 저려서 눈을 감았어요.
examples.en: My knees went weak during the scary movie, so I closed my eyes.

examples.ko: 오금을 구부리고 오래 앉아 있었더니 다리가 아파요.
examples.en: I sat with my knees bent for a long time, and now my legs hurt.

examples.ko: 무릎 뒤 오금에 땀이 나서 불편해요.
examples.en: I'm sweating behind my knees and it's uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 넘어졌을 때 오금을 다쳐서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I hurt the back of my knee when I fell, so I went to the hospital.
The pants ride up to the back of my knees, so it's uncomfortable to walk.
After climbing stairs for so long, the backs of my knees feel stiff.

explain: 무릎 안쪽, 접히는 부분을 가리키는 순우리말이에요. 몸을 설명할 때는 '무릎 뒤쪽'이라고도 말해요. 실제로는 '오금이 저리다'라는 표현으로 가장 많이 들어요.

phrases.example: 높은 다리 위에서 아래를 내려다보니 오금이 저렸어요.
phrases.en: Looking down from a high bridge, my knees went weak with fear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁이 나거나 불안해서 다리에 힘이 빠지고 떨리는 느낌이에요. 무서운 곳이나 위험한 상황에서 주로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes legs losing strength and trembling because of fear or anxiety. It is mainly used about scary places or dangerous situations.

explain_en: It is a native Korean word for the inner, folding part of the knee. When describing the body, people also say '무릎 뒤쪽'. In practice you hear it most in the expression '오금이 저리다'.

examples.en: My stomach pain was bad from the morning, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 위통 때문에 점심을 거의 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: Because of the stomach pain, I could hardly eat lunch.

examples.ko: 위통을 줄이려면 천천히 먹는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To reduce stomach pain, it is good to eat slowly.
After I took medicine, the stomach pain eased.

examples.ko: 위통과 구토가 함께 나타나면 진료를 받으세요.
examples.en: If stomach pain and vomiting appear together, see a doctor.

examples.ko: 위통의 원인을 찾기 위해 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: I had an exam to find the cause of the stomach pain.

explain: 일상에서는 '속이 아파요', '배가 아파요', '속이 쓰려요'처럼 말하는 경우가 많고, '위통'은 병원이나 약 설명에서 잘 나와요. 배 전체가 아픈 '복통'과 달리 위 쪽 통증을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: I ate too much, so my stomach hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '위통' 대신 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural everyday way to say it instead of '위통'.

phrases.en: My stomach burns when I drink coffee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위가 따갑고 아린 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a stinging, burning feeling in the stomach.

phrases.en: After taking medicine, my stomach pain went down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픔이 줄어들 때 쓰고, 설명하는 말투에 잘 맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when pain subsides, fitting an explanatory tone.

explain_en: In daily talk people often say '속이 아파요', '배가 아파요' or '속이 쓰려요', while '위통' shows up in hospital and medicine explanations. Unlike '복통', which is pain in the belly generally, it points to pain around the stomach.

examples.en: A small tumor was found in the test.
The doctor performed surgery to remove the tumor.

examples.ko: 이 종양은 암이 아니라서 걱정 안 해도 돼요.
examples.en: This tumor is not cancer, so you do not need to worry.
The size of the tumor is gradually shrinking.
I was treated for a long time because of a tumor.

examples.ko: 종양에서 조직을 조금 떼어 내 검사해요.
examples.en: They take a small piece of tissue from the tumor and test it.

explain: 몸속 세포가 이상하게 자라서 생긴 덩어리예요. 암인 '악성 종양'과 암이 아닌 '양성 종양'으로 나눠요. '혹'은 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이고, 병원에서 '종양'이라고 하면 더 심각하게 들려요.

phrases.en: The test showed it is a benign tumor, so they say it is okay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 암이 아닌 종양을 말하며 '악성 종양'과 반대예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A non-cancerous tumor, the opposite of '악성 종양'.

phrases.en: A tumor formed in my liver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 종양이 생겼다고 말할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for a tumor appearing in the body.

phrases.en: A small lump appeared on my neck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이고 '종양'보다 덜 심각하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday word that sounds less serious than '종양'.

explain_en: It is a lump formed when cells in the body grow abnormally. Tumors are divided into '악성 종양' (malignant, which is cancer) and '양성 종양' (benign, not cancer). '혹' is the easier everyday word, and hearing '종양' at the hospital tends to sound more serious.

examples.ko: 친구가 다쳐서 수건으로 급하게 지혈을 했어요.
examples.en: My friend got hurt, so I quickly stopped the bleeding with a towel.
The nosebleed wouldn't stop, so I needed to stop the bleeding.

examples.ko: 지혈만 잘해도 큰 사고를 막을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Just stopping the bleeding properly can prevent a serious accident.

examples.ko: 응급 처치에서 가장 먼저 할 일은 지혈이에요.
examples.en: The first thing to do in first aid is to stop the bleeding.

examples.ko: 간호사가 상처를 꾹 눌러서 지혈부터 했어요.
examples.en: The nurse pressed the wound firmly and stopped the bleeding first.

examples.ko: 지혈에는 깨끗한 천으로 누르는 방법이 기본이에요.
examples.en: For stopping bleeding, pressing with a clean cloth is the basic method.

explain: '피가 멎다'는 저절로 멈추는 것이고, '지혈'은 눌러서 멈추게 하는 행동이에요. 보통 '지혈을 하다'나 '지혈하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I pressed on the wound and stopped the bleeding first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지혈'에 '-하다'를 붙인 동사로, 지금 피를 멈추는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 'jihyeol', used for the act of stopping bleeding right now.

phrases.en: After pressing for about ten minutes, the bleeding stopped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동의 결과로 피가 멈춘 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the result: the bleeding has been stopped.

phrases.en: I bought a hemostatic agent at the pharmacy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피를 멈추게 하는 약이나 재료를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a medicine or material that stops bleeding.

explain_en: '피가 멎다' means bleeding stops by itself, while '지혈' is the action of making it stop, for example by pressing. It is usually used as '지혈을 하다' or '지혈하다'.

examples.en: I was tired, so I lay on the bed with my arms and legs stretched out.
The child ran around the yard swinging his arms.
The baby stretched out its arms and legs while sleeping.

examples.ko: 여름이면 모기가 활개를 쳐서 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: In summer, mosquitoes run rampant and I can't sleep.

examples.ko: 사기꾼이 활개 치지 못하게 법을 강화해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to strengthen the law so that fraudsters can't run wild.

examples.ko: 좁은 차 안에서는 활개를 마음껏 뻗기 힘들어요.
examples.en: In a cramped car it's hard to stretch your arms and legs freely.

explain: 원래 사람의 두 팔과 두 다리를 가리키지만 일상에서는 '활개를 펴다', '활개를 치다'처럼 정해진 표현으로만 써요. '활개를 펴고 눕다'는 팔다리를 쭉 뻗는 모습이에요. 비유로는 나쁜 것이 마음대로 퍼질 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 여름만 되면 모기가 활개를 쳐서 잠을 설쳐요.
phrases.en: Every summer mosquitoes run rampant and I lose sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 사람이나 해로운 것이 거리낌 없이 마음대로 퍼지거나 날뛸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when bad people or harmful things spread or act freely without restraint.

explain_en: It originally refers to a person's two arms and two legs, but in daily life it is used almost only in set expressions like '활개를 펴다' and '활개를 치다'. '활개를 펴고 눕다' is lying with limbs stretched out. Figuratively it is also used when something bad spreads freely.

en: to send the wounded or sick to the rear; to transport (patients)

examples.en: The paramedics took the patient to a big hospital.
The helicopter takes the injured person away right away.
How should we evacuate the injured hiker?
The medical team decided to transfer the critical patient to Seoul.
I contacted the rescue team to ask them to evacuate him.
We couldn't evacuate the patient because of the rain.

explain: '옮기다'보다 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스나 보고에서 자주 들려요. 보통 '환자/부상자를 병원으로 후송하다'처럼 대상과 도착지가 같이 나와요. 다친 사람을 주어로 말할 때는 '후송되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The injured person was taken to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 사람이 주어일 때는 피동형 '후송되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the passive form when the injured person is the subject.

phrases.en: They transported the unconscious patient to the emergency room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도착지를 '-(으)로'로 붙이면 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the destination with '-(으)로' sounds natural.

phrases.en: We have to transport the injured person quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어야 하다'를 붙여 급한 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '-아/어야 하다' to express an urgent need.

explain_en: It is more formal than '옮기다' (to move) and often heard in news and reports. It usually comes with the person and the destination, like '환자를 병원으로 후송하다'. When the injured person is the subject, use '후송되다'.

examples.ko: 산 위로 가는 길이 꼬불꼬불 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: The road up the mountain winds on and on.
The alley was so winding that I got lost.
I got a perm yesterday, so my hair is all curly.
The child scribbled wavy letters on the paper.
The river winds its way to the sea.
I like the curly ramen noodles.

explain: '꾸불꾸불'보다 작고 가는 느낌으로, 좁은 길이나 가는 선, 파마머리, 라면 면발에 잘 어울려요. '꼬불꼬불한 길'처럼 뒤에 명사를 꾸밀 수도 있어요.

phrases.en: I climbed the mountain along the winding road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'을 붙여 길을 꾸미는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to describe a road with '-한'.

phrases.en: My hair is curly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파마머리나 곱슬머리처럼 가늘게 꼬인 모양에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for finely curled shapes like permed hair.
phrases.en_equiv: to be curly; to be winding

phrases.en: The river winds along.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼬불꼬불'보다 크고 굵은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels bigger and thicker than 꼬불꼬불.

explain_en: It feels smaller and finer than '꾸불꾸불', and suits narrow paths, thin lines, permed hair and ramen noodles. You can also modify a noun with it, as in '꼬불꼬불한 길'.

examples.en: The plane made a forced landing because of engine trouble.
The news of the forced landing was on the news.
Luckily everyone was safe in the forced landing accident.
The fuel ran out, so a forced landing was unavoidable.
The place of the forced landing was near the sea.
I watched a movie about a spaceship's forced landing.

explain: '불시착'은 계획한 공항이 아닌 곳에 어쩔 수 없이 내리는 일이라 그냥 '착륙'과는 달라요. 비슷한 '비상착륙'은 문제가 생겨 급히 내리는 일 전체에 쓰고, 불시착은 예정에 없던 곳에 내렸다는 점이 두드러져요.

phrases.en: No one was hurt in the emergency landing accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불시착으로 일어난 사고를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an accident caused by an emergency landing.

phrases.en: The plane that made an emergency landing is standing in a field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 '불시착하다'를 이용해 비행기를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the verb form to describe the plane.
phrases.en_equiv: the plane that made a forced landing

phrases.en: The rescue team rushed to the emergency landing site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기가 예정 없이 내린 곳을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Points to the place where the plane unexpectedly came down.

explain_en: A '불시착' is landing at an unplanned place out of necessity, so it differs from an ordinary '착륙'. The similar '비상착륙' covers any urgent landing, while '불시착' stresses landing somewhere that wasn't planned.

examples.en: To get to the island, you have to take the ferry.
The ferry couldn't depart because of the fog.
I checked the ferry timetable at the pier.
For island people, the ferry is more than a simple means of transport.
I ate cup noodles on the ferry while looking at the sea.
I got to the island late on the last ferry.

explain: 바다나 강 건너 두 곳을 이어 주는 배를 말하고, '페리'나 '여객선'과 비슷해요. 요즘 일상 대화에서는 '배'나 '페리'라고 더 자주 하고, '연락선'은 '부관연락선'처럼 옛날 이야기나 역사 글에서도 만나요.

phrases.en: I took the ferry to the island in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연락선'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말로, 배를 이용한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 연락선, meaning to travel by ferry.

phrases.en: Please check the ferry timetable before you leave.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 언제 다니는지 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about when the ferry runs.

phrases.en: You can get to Jeju Island by ferry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 요즘 일상 대화에서는 '연락선'보다 '페리'를 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but 페리 is more common than 연락선 in everyday speech today.

explain_en: It is a boat linking two places across the sea or a river, similar to '페리' or '여객선'. In daily talk people more often say '배' or '페리', while '연락선' also appears in old stories and history writing, as in '부관연락선'.

examples.en: The soldiers secretly entered enemy territory.
Going deep into enemy lines is dangerous.
The soldier who went to scout the enemy position came back.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 혼자 적진에 뛰어들었어요.
examples.en: The hero in the movie jumped into the enemy camp alone.
It took two days to get out of the enemy camp.
In soccer, the striker waits near the opponent's side.

explain: 전쟁뿐 아니라 게임이나 스포츠에서 상대편 진영을 가리킬 때도 써요. '적진에 뛰어들다'처럼 상대의 영역으로 들어간다는 뜻으로 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The soldiers entered the enemy lines at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대 영역에 들어간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means entering the opponent's territory.

phrases.en: The player ran deep into the opponent's side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스포츠에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also common in sports.

phrases.en: He jumped into enemy territory alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 용감하게 위험한 곳에 간다는 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also figurative for bravely entering danger.

explain_en: Besides war, it can mean the opposing side's area in games and sports. It is also used figuratively, as in '적진에 뛰어들다', for entering the other side's territory.

examples.ko: 태풍이 와서 어선 한 척이 전복됐어요.
examples.en: A typhoon hit and one fishing boat capsized.
I heard a truck overturned after slipping on the wet road.
They rescued people from the capsized ship.

examples.ko: 쿠데타로 정부가 전복되고 나라가 혼란에 빠졌어요.
examples.en: The government was overthrown in a coup and the country fell into chaos.

examples.ko: 차가 전복되면 바로 안전벨트를 풀지 마세요.
examples.en: If the car overturns, do not release your seat belt right away.
I watched the moment the long-standing order was overturned.

explain: 전복되다는 배나 자동차가 완전히 뒤집힐 때 쓰고, 정부나 질서가 무너질 때도 써요. 사고 뉴스에서 '배가 전복됐다'처럼 자주 들어요. 같은 소리의 '전복'은 바다에서 나는 해산물이니 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: The car flipped over on the snowy road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전복되다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '전복되다' and common in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 어제 바다에서 배 전복 사고가 났어요.
phrases.en: A boat capsizing accident happened at sea yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used in the news.

phrases.en: The soldiers tried to overthrow the government.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전복되다'는 저절로 뒤집힌 것이고, '전복하다'는 누가 일부러 뒤집는 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '전복하다' is to overturn on purpose, while '전복되다' is to get overturned.

explain_en: It describes a boat or car flipping completely over, and it also describes a government or order being brought down. You hear it often in accident news. A word with the same sound is a seafood (abalone) from the sea, so do not mix them up.
